gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SunGoldPower's own SGR-8K10E kit costs $4,949 today. That is $10 less than the SGR-6510E ChatGPT picked at $4,959, and it comes with the same eight 450 W panels and 10.24 kWh battery but an 8,000 W inverter instead of 6,500 W. No result states either that ChatGPT's $12,476.52 EG4 13 kW kit ships with 27 Canadian Solar 280 W poly panels, while SunGoldPower's SGR-13KM has the same 2× 6.5 kW inverters and 20.48 kWh battery for $9,891.
standout_why: I read the two cited pages and the top result. ecosolarkits.com (cited, checked Oct 26 and Nov 3) gives a price per kWh only for eight SunGoldPower kits, none of them the SGR-8K10E, SGR-6510E or SGR-13KM, and its body and FAQ prices disagree. energysage.com (cited, June 29 prices) lists four kits and no EG4 13 kW kit. preparedstates.com (rank 1) lists 17 kits, including the SGR-10K20E at $8,390, but not the SGR-8K10E, SGR-6510E, SGR-13KM or EG4 KIT-E0003. It gives no price per kWh and names no cell type for any panel. None of these pages compares ChatGPT's five card picks with cheaper versions from the same makers, and none says the EG4 13 kW kit uses old 280 W poly panels.
decides: This changes two of ChatGPT's five picks. (1) The SunGoldPower slot should be the SGR-8K10E, not the SGR-6510E. It is $10 cheaper with the same panels and battery and 1,500 W more inverter output. (2) The 'full-time home' slot (EG4 KIT-E0003, $12,476.52, $609/kWh stored) costs $2,585.52 more than the SunGoldPower SGR-13KM ($9,891, $483/kWh) for the same 13 kW inverter output and 20.48 kWh battery. The EG4 kit does have more panel watts (7,560 W of 280 W poly against 6,300 W of 450 W bifacial N-type). On price per stored kWh, the 20 kWh tier is cheapest with the ECO-WORTHY 10 kW kit ($7,999.99, $391/kWh) and the SunGoldPower SGR-10K20E ($8,390, $410/kWh). The ECO-WORTHY 1560W pick is confirmed: it includes a 5.12 kWh 48 V rack battery, which answers ChatGPT's 'confirm battery capacity' note.
